What that changes about the menu work
My carried belief that "no §16.3 scenario drives either resequencing verb" is stale — Slice 61 closed it by extending scenario 17. The menu enhancement's own open list is empty for the third time, and Stage 6 (comments) is still not startable: two of its four prerequisites stand, and both are yours rather than mine — the REQUIREMENTS.md revision about guest privacy is new intent, and the moderation surface is a slice of real work.

The menu work that is available and is not new intent is the one the plan records at line 1049:

Nothing in this repository measures §11.1 at 375px. Carried from Slice 60. The handheld barrier is scoped to §11.4's surfaces, and the guest menu's box model changed in that slice.

That is Stage 1b's last unclosed surface — the other half of the plan's own title — and it is genuine menu progress. My reading so far:

HandheldReach.MeasureAsync navigates and waits on .page-head, both of which are wrong for §11.1: the guest surface is an interactive island whose measurable state (a chosen dish, an open detail panel, a staged basket line) is arranged by pressing things and would be destroyed by a navigation.
RestaurantInstance.OpenIsolatedPageAsync already takes handheld, so a guest context can be 375×667 for one boolean — but TableJourneys.SeatGuestAsync doesn't forward it.
Scenario 21 already builds most of the arrangement the barrier needs (two dishes, one 86'd, panel open, .order-menu-inspect rendered), which makes "extend rather than add" the same ruling Slices 59, 60 and 61 all made.
.order-menu-choice and .order-menu-inspect both declare min-height: var(--touch-target), and .order-menu is an auto-fit grid with minmax(16rem, 1fr) — 16rem is 256px, comfortably inside 375. So the barrier is unlikely to report on arrival, but I had not yet finished checking .order-basket-controls, .order-send and the two quantity inputs when I hit the tool limit.
